title: Stewards over the revelations must share their gains with Zion
setting: A series of conferences at Hiram, Ohio, ended on 12 November 1831. The last one voted that the revelations were worth the riches of the whole earth to the church. Joseph Smith asked the elders to support those who had worked on the church’s sacred writings. He dictated this revelation that day, possibly in answer to a question. The exact question is not recorded.
summary: The revelation speaks to Zion and to church members far away. It appoints six men as stewards over the revelations: Joseph Smith, Martin Harris, Oliver Cowdery, John Whitmer, Sidney Rigdon, and William W. Phelps. They will give an account of this stewardship at judgment. They are to manage the revelations and their benefits, not give them away. What exceeds their needs goes to the Lord’s storehouse for Zion. No one is exempt from this law, not even the bishop. Stewards over spiritual things deserve support, and all must be equal in temporal things.

contextNote.title: Equality as the condition for the Spirit
contextNote.text: The stewards would earn money from publishing, which raised the question of who should benefit. Verse 7 sends whatever exceeds their needs to the Lord’s storehouse. Verse 10 says no member is exempt, and verse 11 names the bishop and the storehouse agent. Verse 14 then sets the rule that “you shall be equal” in temporal things. It adds a warning that grudging equality would cause the Spirit to be withheld. Verse 13 shows what is at stake: abundance is multiplied “through the manifestations of the Spirit” to those who serve. In this passage, equality is a shared willingness to give, tied directly to spiritual gifts.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 67–70 takes its title from the conference vote behind this revelation. How do verses 7–8 and 14 describe what the stewards owed to Zion?
reviewNote: Read all 18 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 12 November 1831, the last of four conferences and the vote on the revelations’ worth. JSP: may have been dictated during or just after the conference; a later history says it answered an inquiry, but the question is unknown. Inhabitants of Zion mapped to Independence.
